$comment: Where the dashboard is served from, and the extension that may talk to it.
THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE THESE VALUES ARE WRITTEN BY HAND. The extension manifest and
the app both derive from this file — run `npm run sync:extension` after editing it,
and `npm run ci` fails if the two have drifted or if the placeholder below is still
in place. Same arrangement as the firmware and planner snapshots: one source, a sync
step, and a check that makes forgetting it impossible rather than merely unlikely.
localhost is always present and is not configurable. It is what makes `npm run dev`
work against a locally loaded extension. It is also reachable by any other page
served from this machine, which is a real if small exposure: running a local web
server already implies code execution here, and every destructive operation still
requires a native confirmation the page cannot fake. Remove it from
accounts.firebase is the Firebase web app's configuration, pasted from the Firebase console
(Project settings > Your apps > SDK setup and configuration > Config). These values are
public by design: what protects each person's data is firebase/firestore.rules. Leave it
null and the dashboard offers no sign-in at all. accounts.signInProviders lists the sign-in
methods to offer, from google, github, apple, microsoft and password (an email address and
password); each must also be enabled in the Firebase console (Authentication > Sign-in method).
